claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child. My son Alex is 8 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions:

First, are you responsible for Alex? This typically means he lives with you, or you're contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay towards his upkeep if he doesn't live with you full-time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex doesn't actually live with me - he lives with his other parent. But I do contribute towards his upkeep regularly. I help out with money for his needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. To determine eligibility in this situation, I need to understand how much you're contributing.

Are you contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's upkeep? The current Child Benefit rate for one child is £25.60 per week (or about £111 per month). Are you paying at least this amount regularly?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I contribute £30 a week towards Alex's needs - things like clothes, school supplies, and other expenses. So that's a bit more than the Child Benefit amount.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

Now I need to ask: is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? Typically, only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. One more important question:

Do you have immigration permission or the right to live in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, have settled status, or have another type of visa or permission that allows you to be here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm a British citizen, so I have the right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

Is Alex also living in the UK with his other parent?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives in the UK with his other parent.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 8 years old, which is under 16
- **You meet the responsibility test** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £30 per week towards his upkeep, which is more than the Child Benefit amount (£25.60 per week)
- **No one else is claiming** - No one else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- **Residency requirements are met** - You're a British citizen living in the UK, and Alex also lives in the UK

You can proceed with making a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. You'll need to complete a claim form and provide Alex's birth certificate as part of the application process.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit or your claim?
